## VERDICTS ON OPEN REGISTRY ENTRIES

CONFIRM C0163 — `build_feedback_records()` section 1 only iterates `cell_verdicts.items()`. A finding with `final_verdict == "REJECTED"` but no per-cell REJECTED verdicts (e.g. pipeline-level rejection with only UNCERTAIN cells) gets no feedback record. The source at lines 234-256 confirms this: the guard `if refutations or final_v == "REJECTED"` is inside the `for fid, verdict_list in cell_verdicts.items()` loop, so findings absent from `cell_verdicts` are never reached. Same root cause as C0191/C0204/C0224/C0230/C0237.

CONFIRM C0189 — `detect_finding_id_collisions` at line 78 uses `getattr(f, "finding_id", None)` which returns `None` for objects lacking the attribute, filtering them out at line 79. The function is observation-only as designed, but if `findings` contains non-Finding objects (e.g. dicts from JSON deserialization), the `getattr` silently returns `None` and the collision goes undetected. Confirmed as a robustness gap (not critical given the observation-only role).

CONFIRM C0206 — `build_feedback_records()` section 4 (lines 294-317) iterates `rk_validation` as `for model_id, validation_records` but the `model_id` key is unused. The `finding = finding_by_id.get(fid)` lookup uses the finding_id from the validation record, so it finds the correct Finding object. However, `finding.model_id` (used for `model_origin`) is the original authoring model, not necessarily the model whose R_k self-assessment is being checked. If model A's R_k for model B's finding is flagged WARN, the feedback record's `model_origin` points to model B (finding author), not model A (the one whose R_k is wrong). The feedback section then routes to model B, not model A.

CONFIRM C0241 — `parse_admissibility_block()` regex `(PASS|FAIL)` does not match `N/A`. Verified at line 604: the pattern is `pat + r"\s*[:\-=]?\s*(PASS|FAIL)"`. A model reporting `sigma_measured: N/A` will have `found_pass = False, found_any = False`, so `sigma_measured` is added to the failed list. This is the same root cause as C0003/C0184/C0213/C0227.

However, changing `model_origin` on an existing record would be wrong (it would misroute the refutation/admissibility feedback). The current fix is correct: when `rec is None`, the only feedback is R_k, so routing to `rk_model_id` is right.
